final.memo:
Charlie and I have looked at this business, but it belongs firmly in the 'too hard' pile. While the company provides various financial services, its operations are highly sensitive to market liquidity and the confidence of those who fund its day-to-day activities [D01, D06]. We require businesses with durable competitive advantages and predictable economics, yet this firm has demonstrated extreme volatility, with net income falling 57% in the most recent quarter [D01, D03].

Financial institutions that rely on continuous access to credit markets to survive are prone to shocks that make long-term investment hazardous [D05, D06]. When an institution's survival depends on the fleeting sentiment of the market rather than an underlying moat, the risk of permanent loss of capital is too great [D01, D05]. We prefer to hold cash rather than risk our reputation and capital on businesses that do not offer a clear path to normalized owner earnings [D01, D08].
